judge_temperature: default (claude -p does not expose temperature; rubric is identical across runs)

A.comment: Clear directed arrow from the rectangle (Overfitting) to the diamond (High test error) unambiguously encodes causation, and both concepts are named without clutter, but the declared 700×440 canvas dwarfs the actual content—which sits in the top-left corner—and two marker definitions (hollow-tri, bar) are included in <defs> yet never referenced.

B.comment: Both concepts are present with a clean directional arrow conveying causation, but 'High test error' rendered at font-size 12 in a box only 60 px wide will overflow its container and likely clip against the 200-unit viewBox edge, making the right label partially unreadable.

A.comment: Clean left-to-right arrow from 'Wake up' to 'Drink coffee' unambiguously conveys the 'then' sequence in natural reading order.

B.comment: Arrow correctly links the two nodes but the spatial layout is right-to-left (wake up on the right, drink coffee on the left), inverting the natural reading order and undermining the sequential relation; additionally the 700×440 canvas is nearly empty and two marker definitions (hollow-tri, bar) are declared but never used.

per_clause.clause: The arm is part of the body.

A.comment: Arrow with explicit 'is part of' label between 'arm' and 'body' unambiguously encodes the part-of relation with no extraneous elements.

B.comment: Nesting 'arm' inside a 'body' container partially hints at containment but adding a spurious third node labeled 'part' muddies the relation, and the use of <foreignObject> for a plain text label violates the render-validity criterion.

A.comment: The labeled arrow clearly names 'contains' but an arrow conventionally implies causation/flow rather than physical containment, so the visual relation is ambiguous; both concepts are cleanly labeled and the layout is well-spaced with a valid, minimal SVG.

B.comment: Nesting toy inside box is the most direct visual encoding of 'contains', but the SVG misuses <foreignObject> for the box label, carries three entirely unused marker defs, and places small content in the top-left corner of a 700×440 canvas, making the document both wasteful and technically impure.

A.comment: The connecting path carries no arrowhead and no visible label, so the 'has' (possession/part-of) relation is entirely invisible to a viewer despite the data-eid hint buried in an attribute; three marker definitions are declared but never referenced by the edge element, adding dead weight.

B.comment: An arrow from 'body' to 'heart' labelled 'has' unambiguously encodes the stated relation; the SVG is valid and self-contained, though the <defs> block appears after the element that references the marker and HTML-style comments add minor bloat.

per_clause.clause: A dolphin is similar to a whale.

A.comment: The ≈ symbol between double parallel lines is an excellent and unambiguous encoding of 'similar to,' but the 700×440 canvas wastes enormous space on empty whitespace and the defs block defines three markers (arrow, hollow-tri, bar) that are never used anywhere in the diagram.

B.comment: The explicit 'similar to' label paired with a bidirectional connecting line communicates the symmetric relation clearly, though the arrowhead polygons are dimensionally tiny and the HTML-style comments add minor noise to the SVG source.

A.comment: Double-bar terminators are a plausible 'opposition' marker but are non-standard and ambiguous; the entire content occupies roughly 304 × 74 px in a 700 × 440 canvas, wasting most of the space, and two of the three defined markers (arrow, hollow-tri) are never used.

B.comment: Opposing double-headed arrows intuitively convey mutual opposition and the layout is clean and well-proportioned, though HTML-style comments scattered through the markup count as minor decorative noise.

per_clause.clause: A dolphin is an example of a mammal.

A.comment: The labeled arrow 'is example of' from Dolphin to Mammal unambiguously encodes the instance-of relation with both concepts clearly boxed and no extraneous elements.

B.comment: A spurious third node 'example' is reified inside the mammal container, distorting the binary relation; the <foreignObject> escape hatch is used for ordinary text, and several marker definitions go unused, bloating the output.

per_clause.clause: The algorithm uses a binary heap.

A.comment: Solid directional arrow with an explicit 'uses' label leaves no ambiguity about the relation, both concepts are clearly boxed and labelled, spacing is generous, and the SVG is minimal and well-formed.

B.comment: The dashed arrow carries no 'uses' label, making the relation ambiguous; the canvas is 700×440 yet all content is crammed into roughly the top-left 330×90 px corner, leaving most of the viewport empty, and two marker definitions (hollow-tri, bar) are declared but never referenced.

A.comment: Directed arrow explicitly labelled 'requires' makes the relation immediately unambiguous, both concepts are clearly named, layout is clean with no overlap, and the SVG is minimal and valid.

B.comment: The unlabelled hollow-triangle arrowhead conventionally signals UML inheritance/IS-A rather than 'requires', so the relation is visually misleading; additionally the 700×440 canvas is vastly oversized for content occupying roughly 370×74 px, and two of the three defined markers go unused.

A.comment: A directed arrow with an explicit 'reduces to' label between 'Problem' and 'Sorting' unambiguously encodes the reduction relation, and the SVG is compact and clean.

B.comment: The filled triangle wedge between the two boxes is visually ambiguous (not a standard reduction arrow and carries no text label), the meaningful content occupies only the top ~75 px of a 700×440 canvas leaving vast dead space, and three marker definitions (arrow, hollow-tri, bar) are declared but only zero are actually used on any visible element.

per_clause.clause: The perimeter equals four times the side.

A.comment: The equality is suggested by a '=' label over a dashed line, but conflating the multiplier into one node label ('four time side', with a typo) makes the relation ambiguous, and three of the four defined markers go unused, wasting markup.

B.comment: An arrow from 'side' to 'perimeter' labelled '= 4 ×' cleanly encodes the multiplicative equality, both concepts are exactly and clearly named, and the layout is tidy, though HTML comments add minor decorative noise.
